Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
Suffix -tion is /ʃən/ (implementation), -sion after a vowel is /ʒən/ (decision), -ous is weak /əs/ (nervous), and -ly adds a syllable only when the adjective ends in -le or -ble.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Suffixes & Word Formation.

Choose the suffix by the slot, not by the root: after a determiner you need a noun (-tion, -ment, -ness), before a noun you need an adjective (-able, -ive, -ous), and a verb needs -ise, -ify or -en. Then check the spelling shift: decide → decision, maintain → maintenance.

-tion / -sion — verb to noun: implement → implementation
-ment — verb to noun: agree → agreement
-able / -ible — verb to adjective: rely → reliable
-ive — verb to adjective: persuade → persuasive
-ly — adjective to adverb: remarkable → remarkably
-ise / -ify — noun or adjective to verb: modern → modernise, pure → purify
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which is the noun from 'maintain'?
2. Complete: 'The findings are ___ (convince).'
3. Which suffix makes an adverb?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

decide → decision — The decision was taken in June. (Verb to noun with -sion.)
rely → reliable — The source is reliable. (Verb to adjective with -able.)
care → careless — The reply was careless. (Noun to adjective with -less.)
What do you observe?

A suffix fixes the word class: -tion and -ment make nouns, -able and -ive make adjectives, -ly makes adverbs, -ise makes verbs. The same root takes different suffixes with different meanings, and some combinations are lexical, not logical.
1. What class does -ness create?
2. Is 'economical' the same as 'economic'?
options: No: economic concerns the economy, economical means thrifty.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can build word families from roots.

Success criteria:
- I can name the word class each suffix produces.
- I can fill a noun slot with the right derived noun.
- I can check a derived word against the spelling shift.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The decision was implement quickly (noun slot filled by a verb) → ✅ The decision was implemented quickly
❌ She spoke with great confident (adjective where a noun is needed) → ✅ She spoke with great confidence
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The maintenance of the fleet costs more than its purchase.
The argument is persuasive but thin.
The figures were remarkably consistent.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where nominalisation & register carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Nominalisation & Register. Nominalise when the action, not the actor, is the topic: the implementation of the policy took two years. Keep the agent in a possessive when responsibility matters: their refusal
